sections.name: General Knowledge / Current Affairs of India and Goa
Core: Organon, Materia Medica and Pharmacy

p1.title: Passage 1
paras: The slow dismantling of institutionalized stigmas surrounding mental health disorders is a significant cultural shift, yet clinical frameworks still struggle to address the deep structural root causes of psychological distress. For decades, public health messaging focused almost entirely on correcting chemical imbalances within individuals, promoting a pharmaceutical-first model of care. While biomedical interventions remain absolutely vital for millions, this narrow focus risks ignoring the socio-environmental factors—such as economic insecurity, chronic professional burnout, systemic marginalization, and the profound isolation of modern digital life—that drive psychological suffering. True mental healthcare requires moving past simple awareness campaigns toward dismantling the structural barriers that prevent access to care, specifically integrating psychiatric resources into primary public health networks. Furthermore, the growing commodification of "wellness" via digital platforms often reduces mental health care to a superficial aesthetic of self-care, masking the absence of systemic psychiatric support. The ultimate test of societal empathy lies in building accessible, communal, and non-punitive mental health infrastructure that values psychological well-being as a universal human right rather than an individual luxury.

p2.title: Passage 2
paras: Depending on what and how you communicate with others or conduct yourself, you will either draw people close to you or drive them away from you. The largest content of non-verbal communication is contributed by what is popularly called body language. Depending on what this speaks you would get a red-carpet welcome or rejection. Hence, it is important to know where you stand. It is equally important to know the requirements of different situations, time and place to ensure you are able to take care of your own acceptance. In a tradition-ruled country like India, body conduct has an important relevance in valuing relationships and individuals. If your general disposition is good you will readily emit sparks that make you the centre of happenings. Expression of the eye, good eye contact makes your interlocutor feel you are keen to live life. Sensitive people keep changing their expression and literally swing up or down.

questions.q: The author criticizes a purely "pharmaceutical-first model of care" because it:
opts: Risks overlooking the socio-environmental drivers of distress.
Relies too much on primary care.
questions.why: Detail: 'this narrow focus risks ignoring the socio-environmental factors'. Passage: GPSC pre-screening test (Junior Scale Officer), Jun 2026.

questions.q: Which is identified as a socio-environmental factor in mental health?
opts: Economic insecurity and the isolation of digital life.
questions.why: Detail: listed in the third sentence. Passage: GPSC pre-screening test (Junior Scale Officer), Jun 2026.

questions.q: Digital "wellness" platforms can have a negative effect by:
opts: Reducing psychiatric care to a superficial, commercialised aesthetic of self-care.
questions.why: Detail: the fifth sentence. Passage: GPSC pre-screening test (Junior Scale Officer), Jun 2026.

questions.q: A critical step toward systemic mental healthcare, according to the text, is:
opts: Integrating psychiatric resources into primary public health systems.
questions.why: Detail: the fourth sentence. Passage: GPSC pre-screening test (Junior Scale Officer), Jun 2026.

questions.q: The author's conclusion frames psychological well-being as:
opts: A universal human right needing accessible, communal infrastructure.
An individual responsibility managed through apps.
questions.why: Main idea: the last sentence. Passage: GPSC pre-screening test (Junior Scale Officer), Jun 2026.

questions.q: According to the passage, a warm social welcome depends mainly on one's
questions.why: Detail: 'Depending on what this [body language] speaks you would get a red-carpet welcome or rejection'. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Assistant Public Prosecutor), Jun 2025.

questions.q: What is particularly significant in a country like India for being socially accepted, as the passage implies?
questions.why: Detail: 'In a tradition-ruled country like India, body conduct has an important relevance'. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Assistant Public Prosecutor), Jun 2025.

questions.q: Which phrase in the passage means "warm and willing acceptance"?
questions.why: Vocabulary from the passage. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Assistant Public Prosecutor), Jun 2025.

questions.q: The word "interlocutor" in the passage means
questions.why: Vocabulary: the person you are speaking with. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Assistant Public Prosecutor), Jun 2025.

questions.q: Consider: (i) It is important to know how good or bad one's body language is. (ii) Responding to the time, place and situation helps decide one's acceptance. According to the passage:
questions.why: Both are stated: 'know where you stand' and 'know the requirements of different situations, time and place'. Passage: GPSC CBRT (Assistant Public Prosecutor), Jun 2025.

questions.q: Choose the correct conditional sentence:
opts: Were I in your position, I will accept the offer.
If I am in your position, I would accept the offer.
Were I in your position, I would accept the offer.
Was I in your position, I would accept the offer.
questions.why: 'Were I …' is the inverted form of 'If I were …', followed by 'would'. GPSC-style practice item, modelled on the 2026 grammar blocks.

questions.q: Identify the error: “One of my friend has joined the health department.”
questions.why: 'One of' takes a plural noun: 'one of my friends'. GPSC-style practice item, modelled on the 2026 grammar blocks.

questions.q: Choose the correct negative transformation: “Only a fool would say that.”
opts: Only not a fool would say that.
A fool would not say that.
Not a fool would say that.
None but a fool would say that.
questions.why: 'Only' = 'none but' (keeps the meaning). GPSC-style practice item, modelled on the 2026 grammar blocks.

questions.q: Choose the correct modal: “The form is optional; you ______ fill it in.”
questions.why: 'Need not' = no obligation; 'must not' = prohibition. GPSC-style practice item, modelled on the 2026 grammar blocks.

questions.q: Choose the correct preposition: “She is fond ______ classical music.”
questions.why: 'Fond of'. GPSC-style practice item, modelled on the 2026 grammar blocks.

questions.q: The modified UDAN scheme aims to connect how many new destinations over the next decade?
questions.why: UDAN: Ude Desh ka Aam Nagrik. Aug 2026.

questions.q: The GOBARdhan scheme (₹23,731 crore, FY27–FY36) aims to raise tenfold the production of:
Who became the first CEO of the Indian Super League under its new club-led model in 2026?
questions.why: The ISL is India's top football league. Sep 2026.

questions.q: Mayank Chakraborty became India's 94th Grandmaster in 2026 and the first from:
questions.why: Chess.

questions.q: Women's Equality Day is observed on:
questions.why: 13 February is National Women's Day (Sarojini Naidu's birthday).

questions.q: Who was the last Portuguese Governor-General of Goa, who surrendered on 19 December 1961?
questions.why: Operation Vijay.

questions.q: The Defence Research and Development Organisation (DRDO) was formed in:
questions.why: Headquartered in New Delhi.

questions.q: NUCFDC, whose new Mumbai office opened in 2026, is the umbrella organisation for:
questions.why: National Urban Co-operative Finance and Development Corporation.

questions.q: The Nobel Prize in Physiology or Medicine 2026 was awarded for discoveries concerning:
questions.why: Karl Deisseroth, Peter Hegemann and Georg Nagel. Oct 2026.

questions.q: The Sardar Sarovar Dam is built on the river:
questions.why: In Gujarat.

questions.q: Find the next number in the series: 1, 1, 2, 3, 5, 8, 13, ?
questions.why: Each term is the sum of the two before it: 8 + 13 = 21.

questions.q: If '+' means multiply, 'x' means subtract, '-' means divide and '/' means add, what is the value of 8 + 6 x 12 - 4 / 5?
questions.why: After substitution: 8 x 6 - 12 / 4 + 5 = 48 - 3 + 5 = 50.

questions.q: Konkani is to Goa as Malayalam is to:
questions.why: Konkani is the official language of Goa; Malayalam of Kerala.

questions.q: The words Record, Recount, Receipt, Recall and Recent are arranged as in a dictionary. Which word comes third?
questions.why: The order is Recall, Receipt, Recent, Record, Recount.

questions.q: A's mother is the only daughter of B's father. If B is a man, how is B related to A?
questions.why: B's father's only daughter is B's sister. She is A's mother, so B is A's maternal uncle.

questions.q: Town P is 12 km due north of town Q. Town R is 5 km due west of P. What is the shortest distance between Q and R?
questions.why: The two legs are at right angles: the square root of 144 + 25 = 169, which is 13 km.

questions.q: Statement: Should the government ban plastic bags? Arguments: I. Yes, it will significantly reduce pollution and protect marine life. II. No, it will cause job losses in plastic manufacturing and inconvenience consumers.
opts: Both I and II are strong
questions.why: Both give a direct, serious consequence of the policy. GPSC CBRT, Jun 2025.

questions.q: A petroleum product's price rises 25% every odd year and falls 20% every even year. After exactly 8 years the price has
questions.why: × 1.25 × 0.8 = × 1 every two years, so after 8 years it is unchanged. GPSC CBRT, Jun 2025.

questions.q: All X are Y. Some Y are Z. No Z is X. Which is true?
questions.why: 'No Z is X' turns round to 'No X is Z'. GPSC CBRT, Feb 2026.

questions.q: Find the smallest number which leaves remainder 7 when divided by 12, 18, 21 or 30.
'Similia similibus curentur' is correctly translated as:
opts: Likes are always cured by likes
Let likes be cured by likes
questions.why: Hahnemann wrote 'curentur' (subjunctive: let them be cured), a rule for the physician to follow, not 'curantur' (are cured).

questions.q: According to §6, the unprejudiced observer perceives in each individual disease only:
opts: the changes in health of body and mind that can be perceived by the senses
the material cause of the disease
the name given to the disease in textbooks
questions.why: §6: the observer, free from speculation, notices only deviations from the former healthy state, felt by the patient, remarked by those around him and observed by the physician.

questions.q: In Kent's observations, a quick, short and strong aggravation followed by rapid improvement indicates:
opts: a correct remedy and good vitality: the best prognosis
an incurable case with tissue destruction
a wrong remedy that must be antidoted
questions.why: Kent's third observation: the aggravation is quick, short and strong and is followed by rapid improvement, so the remedy suited and the reaction is vigorous.

questions.q: Hahnemann held psora responsible for what share of all chronic diseases?
questions.why: In The Chronic Diseases Hahnemann attributes about seven-eighths of chronic diseases to psora, the rest to syphilis and sycosis.

questions.q: Over-growth, warts, infiltration of tissues and aggravation in damp weather are characteristic of:
questions.why: Sycosis is the miasm of excess and over-production: warts, condylomata, thickening and catarrhal discharges, worse in humid weather.

questions.q: According to §150, a trivial ailment of recent origin (an indisposition) should be handled by:
opts: a slight change in diet and regimen, usually without medicine
an antipsoric remedy in high potency
a nosode of the prevailing miasm
questions.why: §150: a few trivial symptoms observed only a short time are not a fully developed disease; altering the diet and regimen will usually dispel the indisposition.

questions.q: The sixth edition of the Organon was first published, in German, in:
questions.why: Hahnemann finished the manuscript in 1842, a year before his death; Richard Haehl published it in 1921.

questions.q: 'The Genius of Homoeopathy: Lectures and Essays on Homoeopathic Philosophy' was written by:
questions.why: Stuart Close (1860-1929) published The Genius of Homoeopathy in 1924.

questions.q: The first remedy improved the patient; the improvement has stopped and the same symptoms have returned unchanged. The second prescription should usually be:
opts: a repetition of the same remedy
a new remedy chosen from the latest symptoms only
questions.why: Kent: when the original symptoms return unchanged after a good effect, the remedy is still indicated and is repeated.

questions.q: Rheumatic pains that are worse before a thunderstorm are a keynote of:
questions.why: Rhododendron: dread of storms, with pains that come on before a thunderstorm and ease once it breaks.

questions.q: Injuries to the periosteum and tendons, and eyestrain from fine work, call for:
questions.why: Ruta: bruised periosteum, strained tendons and flexors, and aching eyes after close work.

questions.q: Jealousy, obscene talk, a desire to uncover and foolish laughter point to:
questions.why: Hyoscyamus: jealous, immodest and obscene, with silly laughter and twitching.

questions.q: Which remedy is inimical to Rhus toxicodendron?
questions.why: Apis and Rhus tox are inimical and should not follow each other. Bryonia is complementary to Rhus tox.

questions.q: Ill effects of loss of sleep and night watching, with vertigo and nausea from riding in a carriage, call for:
questions.why: Cocculus: exhaustion from nursing the sick through the night, and travel sickness with vertigo.

questions.q: Profound melancholy with thoughts of suicide, and bone pains that are worse at night, indicate:
questions.why: Aurum met.: deep depression with a longing to die, and syphilitic bone pains worse at night.

questions.q: Stitching pains, aggravation between 2 and 4 a.m. and swelling of the upper eyelids are characteristic of:
questions.why: Kali carb.: stitching pains, the 2 to 4 a.m. aggravation, and baggy swelling of the upper lids.

questions.q: Profuse, offensive sweat that brings no relief, aggravation at night, and a moist, flabby, indented tongue with intense thirst point to:
questions.why: Mercurius: worse at night and from the heat of the bed, sweats without relief, and has the moist tongue with thirst.

questions.q: Which of the following is an imponderable?
questions.why: Imponderabilia are drugs prepared from energy, such as X-ray, magnetism and electricity.

questions.q: Nosodes are prepared from:
questions.why: Nosodes come from diseased material, such as Psorinum, Medorrhinum and Tuberculinum. Healthy tissues give sarcodes.

questions.q: By Hahnemann's method, how long does the trituration of one centesimal potency take?
questions.why: Each potency takes one hour: three periods of 20 minutes, each of 6 minutes' grinding and 4 minutes' scraping, done twice.

questions.q: After which trituration did Hahnemann convert a potency into liquid form?
questions.why: After the third centesimal trituration the substance is soluble and is carried on as a liquid potency.

questions.q: How many succussions are given at each step of the LM (50 millesimal) potency?
questions.why: The 6th edition prescribes 100 strong succussions for each LM step. The 5th edition used 2 for centesimal potencies.

questions.q: The first volume of the Homoeopathic Pharmacopoeia of India was published in:
questions.why: HPI Volume I appeared in 1971; further volumes followed.

questions.q: The Drugs and Cosmetics Act, which also governs homoeopathic medicines, was passed in:
questions.why: The Act dates from 1940. The Drugs and Cosmetics Rules followed in 1945.

questions.q: Which of the following is NOT a vehicle in homoeopathic pharmacy?
questions.why: Vehicles are neutral carriers with no medicinal action. Sulphur is a medicinal substance.
